guides.title: Risk Assessment (UK): A Practical Beginner’s Guide
guides.excerpt: What a UK risk assessment is, who needs one, and how to write a simple one that actually helps.
body: A risk assessment is a practical way to identify what could cause harm at work and decide what controls are reasonable.
In the UK, the expectation is that you assess risks and take sensible measures to control them — then keep it under review.
This guide walks you through a simple, repeatable approach and links to a template you can download.
checklist: Describe the task and the setting
Identify hazards (things that can cause harm)
Decide who might be harmed and how

guides.title: COSHH Assessment (UK): How to Do It Properly (Without Overcomplicating It)
guides.excerpt: A practical COSHH assessment flow: substances, exposure routes, controls, and what good looks like on site.
body: A COSHH assessment focuses on health risks from substances (including dusts, fumes, vapours, biological agents, and products from processes).
Good COSHH is mostly: knowing what the substance is, how people are exposed, and putting controls in place that are actually used.
This guide gives you a simple structure and links to a COSHH template pack.
checklist: Identify who is exposed and how (inhalation/skin/ingestion)

guides.title: RIDDOR Explained (UK): What Must Be Reported and How
guides.excerpt: A plain-English guide to what’s reportable, who reports, time limits, and how to avoid common mistakes.
body: RIDDOR is the UK system for reporting certain injuries, diseases and dangerous occurrences.
The easiest way to stay compliant is to build a simple decision process: what happened → is it reportable → who reports → keep records.
This guide includes a quick “is this reportable?” checklist and an incident record template.
checklist: Check if it’s a specified injury, over-7-day, or dangerous occurrence
Confirm who is the responsible person
Keep internal records and complete investigation
Review your risk assessment and training
